China's Animal Epidemic Prevention Law: Article 30 provides for dog owners to have dogs immunized and registered, for dogs taken outside to wear a tag and be on a leash, and for sub-district and township authorities to coordinate with residents' and villagers' committees in controlling and handling stray dogs and cats; Article 31 distinguishes units and personnel involved in the relevant activities, who must report immediately and promptly bring the situation under control, from other persons who find such situations and must report promptly; Article 32 provides for confirmation at or above county level, confirmation at provincial level for major cases and, when necessary, confirmation by the agriculture and rural affairs department of the State Council. Article 11 covers quarantine by animal health supervision bodies, and Article 12 covers animal disease prevention and control bodies undertaking technical work such as monitoring, testing, diagnosis, epidemiological investigation and reporting. Article 29 lists the situations in which slaughtering, trading and transporting are prohibited, with statutory exceptions for centralized harmless storage and transport. Article 4 lists rabies in category two, and Article 14 concerns work injury insurance and subsidies or compensation for disease prevention personnel. entries.answer: Animal control workers correspond to U.S. Animal Control Workers (33-9011), dealing with abandoned, dangerous or unattended animals, investigating abuse and attacks, recording sheltering and handling, and public education. The U.S. tasks list capture, summonses or requests for police arrest, court appearances and euthanasia, which do not directly authorize the same-named job in China. The work of animal control workers falls into four categories: responding to reports and on-site handling (answering public enquiries, arriving after receiving and dispatching a call, using nets, snares or tranquilizer darts to capture and remove stray, out-of-control or abused animals, taking captured animals out of vehicles and putting them into shelter cages, providing food, water and daily care for animals, and cleaning kennels, vehicles and other facilities and equipment); investigation and enforcement (investigating reports of animal attacks or abuse, interviewing witnesses, collecting evidence and writing reports, checking animals for injury or malnutrition and arranging treatment, checking animal licences and whether shelters comply, issuing warnings or summonses for violations or contacting the police to report violations and request arrests, and preparing for prosecution and testifying in court); sheltering, placement and handling (writing activity reports and keeping sheltering and handling files for animals, contacting animal owners to tell them their pet is at the shelter, organizing adoptions of unclaimed animals, euthanizing rabid, unclaimed or severely injured animals, collecting dead animals from roads and disposing of carcasses, and transporting injured or sick wild animals to rescue organizations); and public education and collaboration (educating the public about animal welfare and animal control laws and regulations, running animal safety and wildlife-themed education in schools and community activities, training police officers in dog handling and tracking, crowd control, narcotics detection and explosives detection techniques, and working with the police, animal diagnostic and treatment institutions and shelter organizations). Actual duties in China are verified according to the local statutory division of work, the specific job and its authority; this round did not verify a single Chinese occupation corresponding to U.S. 33-9011, and no claim is made that disease prevention workers or quarantine officers are equivalent. U.S. rabies, unclaimed or severely injured euthanasia tasks do not constitute a lawful basis for handling animals in China. In China, diagnosis and treatment are carried out according to the respective qualifications, filing and scope of veterinarians, assistant veterinarians or rural veterinarians; relevant veterinary students or graduates may assist under the supervision of a veterinarian in accordance with the measures, and institutions need a separate diagnostic and treatment licence. Assistants generally cannot prescribe, write diagnostic certificates or issue certificates, and the provincial exception for independent rural diagnosis and treatment is checked separately. A job title or ordinary training does not confer diagnostic and treatment rights.
